chamber.rule: 51 of 100 seats, or 50 with the Vice President's vote; seats not up and independents counted by caucus

vice_president.note: the model's own chance that the Democrat wins the College, from its forecast on 538's national average of 2024-09-12 (the presidency's p in data/president/2024.json stands under the model's own): states whole, a 269 tie counted half; assumed independent of the Senate's common swing

chamber.seat_model: y_i = mean_i + swing_loading_i * d + e_i, d ~ N(0, common_swing_sd^2), e_i ~ N(0, own_sd_i^2), each seat's stage_two.inputs giving mean, own_sd, swing_loading
chamber.not_up_source: the winner of each seat's latest election before 2024: Cha, Kuriwaki and Snyder from 2006, MEDSL's U.S. Senate 1976-2024 before

model.what: the model's own forecast (data/congress/REPORT.md section 2), fitted on earlier cycles only, from what was known before the election (the orchestrator, 2026-11-07 05:58); no polls are used, so it carries less than forecasters then knew

calibration.note: k = the root mean square of z = (y - mean) / sd over these earlier years' races, each year forecast from its own earlier cycles

model.sd_is: sqrt(national_sd^2 + s_e^2); national_sd = k s_a sqrt(1 + z (Z'Z)^-1 z'), s_e = k s_e_fitted, z = (1, midterm * P, (1 - midterm) * P), P = +1 Democratic president, -1 Republican; k the calibration factor

variant.note: the mean as fitted, normal tails first (no variant of round 5 passed its test for this level; REPORT 2.7)

near_tie.note: each forecast's own calibration gives its multiplier of p (REPORT 2.6)
